1 · VS Code loaded with fixture workspace

VS Code opened with the mcp-board-refresh-ws fixture workspace. The sidebar shows .kanban/ and .vscode/ folders. The Kanban extension is installed.

source live
2 · Command palette open

Opening the VS Code command palette (Cmd+Shift+P) to run the "Open Kanban Board" command.

source live
3 · Typing "Open Kanban Board"

Typing the full command name "Open Kanban Board" to precisely select it over "Add Feature".

source live
4 · Kanban board panel open

The Kanban board panel opened in the editor area. It reads .kanban/features/ and populates columns with the seed cards.

source live
5 · Board loaded with 3 seed cards

The board shows the 3 open seed cards: "User login flow" (In Progress), "Onboarding wizard" (Todo), "Dark mode support" (Backlog). These are the same .md files the backlog-mcp server reads via its kanban-markdown adapter.

source live
6 · New story file written to .kanban/features/

A script (simulating the backlog-mcp server) wrote api-rate-limiting-2026-06-06.md to .kanban/features/. The FileSystemWatcher in the Kanban extension will detect this within milliseconds.

source live
7 · Board refreshed — "API rate limiting" appeared

The board auto-refreshed. The new "API rate limiting" card now appears in the Todo column — no manual refresh. The FileSystemWatcher fired, FeatureRepository re-read the directory, and the webview received the updated feature list.

source live
8 · Status edit in file → card moves to In Progress

Changing status to "in-progress" in the .md file moved the card to the In Progress column. Any tool writing to .kanban/features/ — the MCP server, a CLI script, or a text editor — drives the board live.

source live
